answer: Vesting delays blunt sybil farms: every reward a new identity earns stays locked for, say, 30 epochs, and is clawed back if peers later flag that identity's work as copied or colluding. Like a vine that must root before it bears fruit, a fresh agent cannot cash out quickly. An attacker running 1,000 clones must fund all of them through the full lock while one exposed opal of a ring can burn every linked stake, so cheap ivory-tower fakes become a costly, slow bet.
